reviewed_content.statement: Let $X$ be a **connected** scheme and choose a geometric point $\bar x\to X$. Define the geometric fibre functor $F_{\bar x}$ from finite étale $X$-schemes to finite sets by $F_{\bar x}(Y)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(\bar x,Y)$ (geometric points above $\bar x$), and define $\pi_1(X,\bar x)=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar x})$. Then (1) the stabilizers of points in such fibres form a fundamental system of open subgroups at the identity, defining a group topology on $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$; (2) with this topology $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ is profinite; and (3) the fibre functor, with its canonical continuous $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$-action, is an equivalence from finite étale $X$-schemes to finite discrete continuous $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$-sets.
